question: What is considered the single most effective measure in breaking the chain of infection in medical asepsis?
explanation: Hand hygiene is universally recognized as the single most effective measure in breaking the chain of infection and preventing HAIs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why must hand hygiene be performed immediately after removing gloves?

options.B: Micro-organisms can rapidly multiply in the warm, moist environment inside gloves
options.C: To remove the sticky residue left by powder
options.D: Hospital policy strictly requires dry skin management

explanation: Micro-organisms can rapidly multiply in the warm, moist environment inside gloves, making hand decontamination critical once they are removed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of wearing medical gloves in clinical practice?

options.A: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene
options.B: To create a physical barrier against potential pathogens
options.C: To keep the hands warm during surgical procedures
options.D: To prevent needle-stick injuries from sharp instruments

explanation: The primary purpose of medical gloves is to create a physical barrier to minimize the risk of contamination from blood, body fluids, and pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: When should a nursing student change their gloves during patient care?

options.A: Only at the end of the entire shift
options.B: When moving from a clean body site to a contaminated body site on the same patient
options.C: Never, as long as they remain visibly clean
options.D: Only when requested by the patient

explanation: Gloves must be changed between different care tasks when moving from a contaminated site to a clean body site to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which type of gloves is appropriate for routine patient care activities like administering a bed bath or handling non-intact skin?
explanation: Examination (non-sterile) gloves are utilized for routine patient care activities involving contact with mucous membranes or non-intact skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why must a nurse use sterile surgical gloves instead of examination gloves for catheter insertion?

options.A: Surgical gloves are cheaper to purchase
options.C: Surgical gloves prevent introducing micro-organisms into sterile body cavities
options.D: Examination gloves are always too large for the hands

explanation: Sterile surgical gloves are required for sterile interventions to prevent introducing pathogens directly into sterile body spaces like the bladder. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which glove material offers exceptional puncture resistance and is completely free of natural rubber latex allergens?
explanation: Nitrile gloves are made from synthetic copolymer, providing exceptional puncture resistance and durability while being entirely latex-free. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is a major clinical limitation associated with natural rubber latex gloves?

options.A: They dissolve instantly when exposed to water
options.B: They can trigger allergic reactions ranging from contact dermatitis to anaphylaxis
options.D: They are completely impermeable to all chemical agents

explanation: The rising prevalence of latex allergies, which can manifest as contact dermatitis or severe anaphylaxis, is a major limitation of natural rubber latex. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: When donning sterile gloves, which part of the first glove is safe to touch with your bare hand?

options.D: The very tip of the fingers

explanation: You should pick up the first glove by touching only its inside folded cuff surface to prevent contaminating the sterile exterior. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: What action must a student nurse take if a sterile glove touches an unsterile surface during the donning process?

options.A: Wipe it down with alcohol-based hand rub
options.B: Continue using it if it looks clean
options.C: Discard the contaminated glove and start over with a new pair
options.D: Cover it with an examination glove

explanation: If any part of a sterile glove touches an unsterile surface, it is considered contaminated and must be discarded immediately. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: During glove doffing, what technique prevents the contaminated outer surface from touching the nurse's bare skin?

options.A: Pulling the gloves off quickly by the fingertips
options.B: Turning the gloves inside out as they are peeled off
options.C: Washing the gloved hands with soap before removal
options.D: Cutting the gloves off with medical shears

explanation: Peeling the gloves off while turning them inside out traps the contaminated outer surface safely on the inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is a major hazard of snapping gloves off forcefully during removal?

options.A: It tears the waste bin liner
options.B: It can aerosolize infectious droplets into the air and onto surrounding surfaces
options.C: It permanently damages the nurse's skin
options.D: It causes the gloves to become sterile again

explanation: Snapping gloves off forcefully can aerosolize infectious droplets, spreading pathogens into the air and onto nearby environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following practices regarding medical gloves is strictly incorrect and promotes cross-contamination?

options.B: Washing and reusing single-use disposable gloves
options.C: Performing hand hygiene after glove removal
options.D: Selecting the correct glove size for the procedure

explanation: Gloves are single-use disposable items and must never be washed, disinfected, or reused under any circumstances. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: What can happen to gloves if they are worn for extended periods or exposed to incompatible substances like oils?

options.B: They can develop microscopic tears, pinholes, or degradation
options.C: They change color to indicate contamination

explanation: Gloves can develop microscopic tears, pinholes, or degrade over time and with exposure to certain substances, compromising their barrier function. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: Under standard precautions, when must gloves be worn?

options.A: Only when caring for patients diagnosed with HIV
options.B: Whenever there is anticipated contact with blood, body fluids, non-intact skin, or mucous membranes
options.C: Only during surgical operations in the theater
options.D: When conversing with patients at the bedside

explanation: Standard precautions require gloves whenever contact with blood, body fluids, non-intact skin, or mucous membranes is anticipated for any patient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)

question: What is the proper protocol for glove use when entering a room for a patient placed on Contact Precautions?

options.A: Gloves are only needed if drawing blood
options.B: Gloves must be donned upon entering the room and removed before leaving
options.C: Gloves can be worn continuously across multiple contact precaution rooms without changing
options.D: Gloves are unnecessary if gowns are already worn

explanation: For patients under Contact Precautions, gloves must be donned upon entering the room and safely removed before leaving, followed by hand hygiene. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)
